domain_restrictions: S is an additive submonoid of ℤ_{≥ 0} (closed under addition and contains 0)
S is cofinite in ℤ_{≥ 0} (so ℤ_{≥ 0} \ S is finite, hence genus(S) is finite)
genus(S) is defined as the number of nonnegative integers not in S: genus(S) := |ℤ_{≥ 0} \ S|
k is restricted to k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 0 because genus is a count of excluded nonnegative integers
For the explicit families described for genus 1 and 2, the intended domain is ℤ_{≥ 0} and set descriptions are of the form {0} ∪ {n : n ≥ m} (and similarly with {2})
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Let S range over numerical semigroups S ⊆ ℤ_{≥ 0} that are cofinite additive submonoids containing 0, and let genus(S) := |ℤ_{≥ 0} \ S|. Then: (1) genus(S)=0 iff S=ℤ_{≥ 0}. (2) genus(S)=1 iff S={0} ∪ {n ∈ ℤ_{≥ 0} : n ≥ 2}. (3) genus(S)=2 iff S equals one of the two sets: A={0} ∪ {n ∈ ℤ_{≥ 0} : n ≥ 3} or B={0,2} ∪ {n ∈ ℤ_{≥ 0} : n ≥ 4}. Consequently, N(0)=1, N(1)=1, N(2)=2, and therefore N(2) ≥ N(1)+N(0) (indeed N(1)+N(0)=2).
quantifier_order: For k ∈ ℕ, k ≥ 0: define N(k) as a cardinality over S
For each genus level g ∈ {0,1,2}: (i) uniqueness/exactness statements about all S with genus(S)=g

variables.role: genus parameter indexing the function N(k)

variables.name: S
variables.role: a cofinite additive submonoid of ℤ_{≥ 0} containing 0, used to define genus(S)

witness_dependencies: In the genus-0 case, the existential witness is unique implicitly: there exists exactly one S with genus(S)=0, namely S=ℤ_{≥ 0}.
In the genus-1 case, existence/witness for S is fixed by the explicit set {0} ∪ {n ∈ ℤ_{≥ 0} : n ≥ 2}; uniqueness means any S with genus(S)=1 must equal this witness.

In the genus-2 case, the witnesses for S are exactly two explicit sets: (A) {0} ∪ {n : n ≥ 3} and (B) {0,2} ∪ {n : n ≥ 4}. Any S with genus(S)=2 must equal A or B, and each of A and B must indeed have genus 2.

statement_nl: Let N(k) denote the number of numerical semigroups of genus k, where a numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers containing 0 and the genus is the number of nonnegative integers not belonging to it. Then the unique genus-0 numerical semigroup is the whole set of nonnegative integers, the unique genus-1 numerical semigroup is the set consisting of 0 together with every integer at least 2, and the genus-2 numerical semigroups are exactly two sets: the set consisting of 0 together with every integer at least 3, and the set consisting of 0, 2, together with every integer at least 4. Consequently N(0) = 1, N(1) = 1, N(2) = 2, and N(2) >= N(1) + N(0).
